messages:
sam: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change landed on canary I see a regression in end-to-end tail latency for the TP=2 PP=4 baseline. Nsight timeline shows recurring GPU idle gaps between pipeline stages that line up with all-reduce windows. Not a complete outage but 25-40% worse p99.

lucy: Thanks. Do you have an nsys capture? Could be padding introduced by the new fused-attn kernel that increases small-batch kernel latency, causing downstream pipeline backpressure.

sam: Uploaded nsys zip to the run artifacts: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/runs/2123456/nsys.zip
Capture notes: 8 microbatches, global batch 64. Kernel-selector picked fused_gemm_attn_v2 for sequence=1024.

yun: Quick nvprof spot-check I ran shows frequent cudaMemcpyAsync -> cudaEventSynchronize patterns around the all-reduce calls. That suggests we might be inserting implicit stream synchronizations in the new kernel path.

mike: Can you paste the nvprof / custom-timer lines? I want to compare with our KV cache timers.

sam: Paste of our custom timers (trimmed):
```
CUSTOM_TIMER total_infer 1234.5ms
CUSTOM_TIMER forward_attn_fused_gemm 9.8ms
CUSTOM_TIMER forward_attn_old_kernel 4.1ms
CUSTOM_TIMER kvcache_lookup 0.9ms
CUSTOM_TIMER microbatch_allreduce 5.6ms
CUSTOM_TIMER stage_idle_gap 12.2ms
```
Notice stage_idle_gap spikes right after forward_attn_fused_gemm in the timeline.

lucy: That lines up with what I see in Nsight — the fused kernel launches extra workspace allocs which cause driver synchronization on older CUDA versions. Which CUDA/cuBLAS were the canary nodes on?

sam: Canary nodes on image: rwinf/cuda12.2-cuBLAS234, non-canary still on cuda12.1. Rollout included selector flag enable_kernel_fused_attn=true.

yun: Two actionable hypotheses: 1) fused_gemm_attn uses temporary host pinned alloc leading to implicit sync; 2) batching heuristic increased microbatch padding (we added per-slot padding to align with warp sizes) and that causes microbatch misalignment across TP ranks so all-reduce waits.

mike: For (2) we should check our Batcher logs. There's a debug switch to emit per-microbatch padding lengths. Run:
```
RWINF_BATCHER_DEBUG=1 ./bin/runtime --workload=tp2pp4 --emit-batch-logs > batchlog.txt
```
I can correlate with the KV cache index map.

sam: I ran that, snippet:
```
batch 0: microbatch_sizes [8,8] padded_sizes [8,8]
batch 1: microbatch_sizes [7,9] padded_sizes [8,8]  <-- padding introduced
```
So we are forcing padding to 8 causing imbalance across ranks.

lucy: Oof — that explains temporary all-reduce skew. When rank A sends less useful tokens and gets padded, rank B finishes earlier and hits an all-reduce wait window.

yun: Quick mitigation: revert kernel-selector flag on canary, and disable per-slot padding heuristic for TP runs until we fix. Could also try reordering padding to be applied symmetrically across TP ranks, but that is more invasive.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Reverted feature flag enable_kernel_fused_attn on canary cluster at 2026-03-16T14:10Z per rollback request.

sam: After revert, tail p99 dropped back to expected baseline in two runs. But we still should fix both: kernel path sync and padding algorithm.

mike: Next steps: 1) lucy to file kernel sync repro and minimal repro case, include nsys and nvprof captures. 2) yun to add cross-rank padding symmetry test to the batching unit tests and add an assertion in the batcher that padded_sizes sum is equal across TP groups. 3) I’ll add a lightweight KV-cache timer delta in the agent to detect stage_idle_gap > 6ms for more than 5% of microbatches.

lucy: Filing kernel issue now with repro script + nsys: https://rwinf/issue/INF-2461 — includes capture and a small C++ repro that shows cudaStreamWaitEvent on workspace alloc.

yun: Adding test in PR: https://rwinf/pull/8342 (WIP) — it fails reproducibly on a small emulated TP harness.

sam: Thanks. Also note: add nvtx markers around allreduce + post-kv-lookup in next debug build so future Nsight timelines make the gap attribution obvious.

mike: Agreed. Add markers like:
```
NVTX_MARKER("kvcache_lookup_start");
...
NVTX_MARKER("kvcache_lookup_end");
NVTX_MARKER("allreduce_start");
...
NVTX_MARKER("allreduce_end");
```
That will make the waterfall view immediate.

sam: Perfect. If everyone can ack the action items here I’ll close the thread and triage the infra rollout plan for the full fleet.

lucy: ack

yun: ack

mike: ack
